summary.headline: Test a narrowly scoped SME cyber-hygiene service before building software.
summary.best_opportunity: Fixed-scope cyber-hygiene and evidence-pack setup with optional monthly maintenance.
summary.why_now: The UK government's 2025 Cyber Security Breaches Survey reports 43% of businesses (about 612,000) identified a breach or attack in the previous 12 months. This supports the presence of a problem, not willingness to buy this specific service; validate with paid pilots.

top_opportunities.name: SME cyber-hygiene setup and monthly check-ins
top_opportunities.description: A fixed-scope baseline of MFA, backups, access and incident-readiness, with a concise evidence pack and separately priced recurring review. Do not claim certification or penetration testing.
top_opportunities.why_now: GOV.UK's 2025 survey says 43% of businesses, approximately 612,000, identified a breach or attack in the prior year; prevalence fell from 50% in 2024, so avoid overstating a growing trend.
top_opportunities.buyer: Micro and small professional-services firms, charities and local businesses without dedicated IT/security staff.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: Approximately £100–£600 for basic tooling, travel and initial professional/insurance advice; validate actual costs before committing.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks via direct outreach and a paid baseline pilot; estimate, not verified conversion data.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium-high if buyers retain monthly checks, onboarding and evidence upkeep; retention unproven.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High for a software engineer with systems skills; keep scope to configuration and documentation within competence.
risks: Liability and trust barriers; define boundaries, obtain suitable advice and insurance, and refer specialist remediation.
Survey prevalence does not prove demand for this offer or willingness to pay.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best low-build-cost test: offer practical hygiene, make no security guarantees, and require paid-pilot evidence before scaling.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-enquiry follow-up automation for one local-service niche
top_opportunities.description: Set up consent-aware enquiry capture, rapid acknowledgement, quote reminders and booking hand-off using the customer's existing tools, with human oversight.
top_opportunities.why_now: A focused service can be sold against a measurable operational problem, but this run found no reliable current UK statistic for missed-lead losses or niche adoption; treat demand as a hypothesis.
top_opportunities.buyer: Trades firms, independent clinics or small agencies receiving repeat enquiries and quotes.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: Approximately £100–£500 for a demo and tools, excluding client-specific subscriptions.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks if a local buyer accepts a paid setup; unverified estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium: monthly monitoring, edits and support are possible; tie them to clear service levels.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High: integrations and workflow design use software-engineering skills.
risks: Each niche may already have capable CRM automation; differentiate on setup speed and outcomes.
Poor integrations, privacy/marketing-consent mistakes or unreliable automation can damage client trust.
top_opportunities.verdict: Good second test if a niche buyer can quantify leads lost or admin time spent; sell a manual-assisted pilot before productising.

top_opportunities.name: Website care and conversion improvements for local businesses
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-price repairs, performance/accessibility basics, analytics and enquiry-form improvements, followed by a modest monthly maintenance plan.
top_opportunities.why_now: A direct service is straightforward to demonstrate and invoice, but no fresh market-size or buyer-demand signal was established in this run.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local professional services and trades businesses with visibly outdated or unreliable sites.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: Approximately £50–£400 using existing development equipment and standard test/hosting tools.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially days to several weeks through targeted audits and direct sales; not verified.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium: hosting coordination, updates and reporting can recur, but commoditisation and churn are risks.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High for a solo software engineer able to deliver web work directly.
risks: Crowded market and price competition; target a specific business type and measurable fixes.
Client access, scope creep and third-party platform issues can erode margins.
top_opportunities.verdict: Fast to offer with little capital, but compete on a narrow outcome rather than generic website building.

top_opportunities.name: AI-assisted admin automation for small professional firms
top_opportunities.description: Map one repeat workflow such as document intake or meeting follow-up, implement a human-reviewed automation using existing tools, and document exceptions.
top_opportunities.why_now: The service can be tested without building a SaaS product, but no robust live UK adoption statistic or evidence of willingness to pay for this exact offer was obtained.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small accountancy, recruitment or consultancy firms with repetitive document and follow-up work.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: Approximately £100–£700 for prototypes and initial tool usage; client subscriptions should be client-funded.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 2–4 weeks after workflow discovery and a paid pilot; estimate only.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Medium-high where monitoring and workflow changes are ongoing and valued.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High for integration, software and testing skills; requires careful data handling.
risks: Errors, sensitive data exposure and changing AI-provider terms require human review and safeguards.
Generic AI automation is easy to imitate; quantify one workflow's time or error reduction.
top_opportunities.verdict: Proceed only after a buyer confirms a costly, repetitive workflow and agrees to a bounded paid test.

top_opportunities.name: Niche local lead-generation site with paid referrals
top_opportunities.description: Build a simple local landing page and directory for one underserved service area, qualify enquiries and charge participating providers for agreed leads.
top_opportunities.why_now: Low-cost web skills make a small test feasible, but this run found no live evidence of a specific underserved geography, search volume or provider willingness to pay.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local service providers in a narrowly defined, higher-value category.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: Approximately £100–£600 for domain, hosting, content and tightly capped promotion.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Usually uncertain and likely slower than direct services; first revenue depends on traffic and provider agreements.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Potentially medium through monthly listings or lead fees if qualified demand is sustained.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High technically, but distribution and sales are the main work.
risks: Search ranking and lead volume are uncertain and may take months.
Lead quality disputes, privacy obligations and acquisition costs can undermine unit economics.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not build broadly; first obtain provider commitments and test a single geography/category with a strict spend cap.

best_pick.name: SME cyber-hygiene setup and monthly check-ins
best_pick.why_it_wins: It combines a credible UK problem signal with low initial build requirements, a service-led route to early payment and a plausible maintenance retainer. The survey validates reported incidents, not demand for this offer, so paid validation is essential.
validation_plan: Interview 10 local micro/small firms about MFA, backup and incident-readiness gaps; ask what they have already paid to address them.
Offer a clearly bounded paid baseline to three qualified firms; proceed only if at least one buys and scope, liability and delivery effort remain acceptable.
best_pick.first_offer: A fixed-price, clearly scoped cyber-hygiene baseline and written action/evidence pack; exclude penetration testing, certification and guarantees, and refer specialist work.
best_pick.mvp: A repeatable checklist, short findings template, secure evidence-handling process and manually delivered follow-up; no software build until repeat use is demonstrated.
customer_types: Small professional-services firms without dedicated security staff
Local charities or other small organisations with basic account and backup needs
best_pick.do_today: Contact five local business owners or advisers, ask about recent practical security checks, and try to book one discovery call without promising compliance or protection.
